name: Rice Kheer
description: Creamy Pakistani rice kheer slowly simmered with basmati rice, full-fat milk and cardamom, then finished with nuts for a rich but spoonable texture.
ingredients: ¼ cup basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 20–30 minutes
½ cup sugar, or to taste
method: Drain the soaked rice. Pour the milk into a heavy-bottomed pot and bring it gradually to a gentle simmer, stirring across the base so the milk does not scorch.
Add the drained rice and crushed cardamom. Cook over low to medium-low heat, stirring regularly, until the rice becomes very soft and the milk reduces noticeably.
Lightly mash some of the softened rice against the side of the pot and stir it back in; this releases starch and thickens the kheer naturally without needing a separate thickener.
Add the sugar only after the rice is tender. Stir until dissolved, then continue simmering gently because the sugar can loosen the mixture temporarily.
Add most of the almonds and pistachios and cook briefly until the kheer is creamy but still slightly looser than your final target, since it thickens further while cooling.
Turn off the heat and add rose water if using. Serve warm, or cool promptly and refrigerate before serving chilled, garnished with the remaining nuts.
tips: Use a heavy pot and stir frequently, especially near the end, because milk can scorch easily.
Kheer thickens further as it cools, so stop cooking while it is slightly looser than your final desired consistency.
storage: Cool leftover kheer promptly, keep it covered and refrigerated, and discard it if it has been left unrefrigerated for an unsafe length of time.
